'''''Jasminum azoricum''''', the '''lemon-scented jasmine''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the olive [[family (botany)|family]].
It is an [[evergreen]] twining [[vine]] native to the Portuguese island of [[Madeira]].<ref name=botanica>{{cite book|editor1=R. G. Turner Jr.|editor2=Ernie Wasson|title=Botanica: The Illustrated A-Z of Over 10,000 garden plants|edition=3rd|year=1999|publisher=Barnes and Noble inc.|page=[https://archive.org/details/botanicaillustra0000unse/page/488 488]|isbn=0-7607-1642-0|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/botanicaillustra0000unse/page/488}}</ref><ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN | accessdate=8 January 2013}}</ref><ref name=tpl>{{ cite web |url=http://www.theplantlist.org/tpl/record/kew-351737|title='''Jasminum azoricum'' L.|work=The Plant List; Version 1. (published on the internet) |year=2010 |access-date=6 January 2013}}</ref> The compound leaves consist of 3 bright green leaflets.<ref name=botanica/> The fragrant white star-shaped flowers appear in [[panicle]]s from the leaf axils in summer, evolving from deep pink buds.<ref name=botanica/><ref name=register/>

The species is critically endangered in its native Madeira. Reports of remaining populations vary between 6 and 50 individual plants in two separate areas, [[Funchal]] and [[Ribeira Brava, Madeira|Ribeira Brava]].<ref name="iucn status 11 November 2021" />
 
''Jasminum azoricum'', which does not tolerate freezing temperatures,<ref name = RHSPF/> has long been in cultivation in Europe as a greenhouse plant with records in Netherlands since 1693 and England from about 1724.<ref name=register/> It has been prized for its bright evergreen foliage, long flowering period and scented blooms.<ref name=register/>  Plants are readily propagated from [[cutting (plant)|cuttings]] and by [[layering (horticulture)|layering]].<ref name=register>{{cite book|author1=Sydenham Teast Edwards|author2=John Lindley|title=The Botanical Register: Consisting of Coloured Figures of Exotic Plants Cultivated in British Gardens with Their History and Mode of Treatment|url=https://archive.org/details/botanicalregist06edwagoog|access-date=8 January 2013|year=1815|pages=[https://archive.org/details/botanicalregist06edwagoog/page/n396 92]–}}</ref> The species prefers a sunny, frost-free position with support from structures such as fences or posts.<ref name=botanica/>

In the [[UK]] this plant has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web 
| url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/23662/i-Jasminum-azoricum-i/Details | title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Jasminum azoricum'' 
| access-date=14 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf 
| title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 56 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society 
| access-date = 14 March 2018}}</ref>
